title: Plate III — The eye of the volute

checks.title: Every tone is tied to a form under the one light
checks.value: 0 of 149 hatch strokes without a form
checks.why: One light per plate, declared (research 02 §11). Tone not tied to a form cannot be proved against it.
checks.fix: Lay tone with hatch({ form }) so each stroke records its form and target tone.

checks.title: Ink follows the light on “egg-1”
checks.why: Darker target tone must carry more ink everywhere on the form; Leonardo ¶555: shadow first on the part away from the light.
checks.fix: Check the form’s normals and the plate light; do not hand-place hatching that the light does not ask for.

checks.title: The lit side of “egg-1” stays paper
checks.why: Where the light falls the paper is the light; ink there flattens the form.

checks.title: Contours are heavy away from the light
checks.why: The quill contour swells where the edge turns from the light (research 01 §1: variable weight).
checks.fix: Draw outlines with contour(), which weights pressure by the light.

checks.title: Dimension dim-height says what the ink measures
checks.why: Nothing on a plate is invented (codex step 2); a value is measured from the drawing, never typed.
checks.fix: Let dimension() compute the value, or correct the geometry, not the label.

checks.title: Extension lines of dim-height: gap and overshoot
checks.why: ISO 129-1 / ASME as cited in research 03 §2.2.

checks.title: dim-height measures the visible ink
checks.target: both ends within 0.8 mm of ink
checks.why: Measure to the visible ink or a stated datum, never to the bounding box (research 03 R9).

checks.title: dim-height stands clear of the drawing
checks.why: Research 03 §2.2: first dimension line 10–12 mm out, tiers 6–10 mm apart.

checks.why: ISO 129-1 / ASME as cited in research 03 §2.2.

checks.why: Measure to the visible ink or a stated datum, never to the bounding box (research 03 R9).

checks.title: dim-eye stands clear of the drawing
checks.why: Research 03 §2.2: first dimension line 10–12 mm out, tiers 6–10 mm apart.

checks.title: The plate states a unit or module
checks.target: a scale bar or a dimension
checks.why: Every plate states a unit or module, or shows a familiar object at scale (research 01 R13, 02 R13).

checks.title: Every fact on the plate has a source
checks.why: If it is not in the truth table it is not on the sheet (codex step 2).

checks.title: Line width breathes (not a plotter, not chaos)
checks.why: Taper and variable weight are the defining marks of the hand (research 01 §1); constant width is the plotter tell.

checks.title: The hand trembles a little, where it is slow
checks.why: Physiological tremor (8–12 Hz) shows on slow strokes; none at all is a plotter, too much is a costume wobble.

checks.title: Strokes enter and leave like a pen
checks.why: A quill lands on its weight, tapers or hooks as it leaves (research 01 §1); butt ends read as plotted.

checks.title: Each surface keeps its own direction
checks.why: A different angle for each adjacent part, regular within it (research 02 §11, R9).

checks.title: Hatching is laid by hand, not by machine
checks.why: Equal gaps and equal lengths are the screen of a plotter.

checks.title: Few colours: ink, construction, overlay
checks.why: Monochrome ink on a light ground plus at most one accent (research 01 R12); many colours or effects is a named fake (01 §5).

checks.title: The modern line is exact
checks.why: Overlay: one hue, true segments and arcs, no jitter, texture or filter (research 03 R1, R3). The drawing keeps the hand; the line keeps its precision.

checks.title: Outline > interior > construction
checks.why: Line weight hierarchy (research 02 R14).

checks.title: A fresh dip shows, sometimes
checks.why: The dip rhythm is the clock of a pen drawing: dark after the dip, paler as it drains.

checks.title: Contours land where they are meant to (near, not on)
checks.why: A hand lands a joined line a hair short or a hair past; exactly on is a plotter, far off is a broken drawing.

checks.title: Every construction generated something
checks.why: Construction appears only if it generated the drawing (research 01 R11); ornamental circles and spirals are a named fake (01 §5).

checks.title: Leaders never cross
checks.why: ISO 128-22 / research 03 R4–5: no free ends, no crossings.

checks.title: Lettering meets ISO 3098 sizes
checks.target: notes and dimensions ≥ 2.5 mm; nothing under 1.8 mm
checks.why: ISO 3098 heights; print ≥ 2.5 mm (research 03 §2.5, §8).

checks.title: Lettering holds 11 px on a 390 px phone
checks.value: 38 of 38 fall under 11 px (sheet shown at 1.39 px/mm)
checks.target: 0, or a phone layout that moves them out
checks.why: Anything under ~11 px at phone width goes outside on a leader, per breakpoint (research 02 C2).

checks.title: No two labels touch
checks.why: Each letter in clear space (research 02 R5).

checks.title: Letters sit on clear paper, never on hatching
checks.why: Letters sit in clear space, never on hatching or lines; otherwise outside on a leader (research 02 R5).

checks.title: Every label is on the sheet
checks.why: A label off the sheet is lost.

checks.title: Mirror script always has a readable twin
checks.value: 0 mirror texts, 0 without a readable twin
checks.why: Notes are readable, non-mirrored, true (research 01 R9); pseudo-mirror writing is a named fake (01 §5).

checks.title: One key system, few labelled parts
checks.why: Capitals for up to ~8 parts, numerals beyond, never mixed (research 02 R4); at most 7 labelled items (03 R12).

checks.title: Lettering reads against the paper
checks.why: WCAG 1.4.3; measured on the rendered pixels when a proof is run (codex KC-8: estimates lied once).

checks.title: Ink wicks into the sheet as much as this paper allows
checks.target: ≤ 30 per 100 mm on sized paper; length ≤ 0.35 mm
checks.why: Feathering follows fibres and sizing; it stays local (founder, ideas/studio-dawn/ink-bleed.md: only the nearby area).

checks.title: Bleed stays near its line
checks.why: When ink scatters it does not affect the overall area, only the nearby (founder).

checks.title: Bleed varies with the sheet (not a filter)
checks.why: Uniform bleed is a filter look; real bleed follows absorbency, load and fibre.

checks.title: Chalk, graphite and metalpoint never pool or feather
checks.value: 0 dry marks with pools or feathers
checks.why: Dry media sit on the tooth; they have no liquid to move.

checks.title: Blots are events, not decoration
checks.why: Blots everywhere are costume; none at all is a plotter.

checks.title: The drawing keeps its margins
checks.why: Rule the sheet first: margins, subject zone, key and notes zones (research 02 R1).

checks.title: The weight of the ink sits at or above the middle
checks.value: ink centroid at 53% of the height
checks.why: The codex “rise”: the sheet carries its weight high (kiruk-codex check.mjs; KC rows). Measured here as the ink-weighted centroid.

checks.title: The sheet is balanced left to right
checks.value: ink centroid at 48% of the width
checks.why: The subject is centred and largest; commentary frames it (research 02 R2).

checks.title: White space is reserved on purpose
checks.why: Main figure first, details around it, white space reserved (research 01 §2, R8); collage density is a named fake (01 §5).

checks.title: The plate says what it explains
checks.value: “A volute is twelve quarter-circles struck from twelve centres inside its eye; each centre lies on the last arc’s end radius, so the scroll turns without a corner.”
checks.why: Claim first (codex): the drawing shows what it is; the line shows why it works.

checks.title: The eye motif is drawn, or its absence justified
checks.value: drawn: the oculus of the Ionic volute — the eye from which the scroll is struck
checks.why: Non-negotiable 4 (CLAUDE.md §5).

checks.title: An explanatory device, not a pretty view
checks.value: construction and build-up, with an enlargement of the eye (×6)
checks.target: section · exploded · build-up · phase · side-by-side · thread · construction
checks.why: Choose the device by what must be explained (research 01 R4); one pretty 3/4 view with arrows is a named fake (01 §5).

checks.title: Finish is selective; the process shows
checks.value: 6 of 6 forms toned; 56% of the construction stands bare
checks.target: some parts left at line or construction; construction visible
checks.why: Everything finished to the same degree is a named fake (research 01 §5, ¶579); kiruk shows its process (CLAUDE.md §2).

checks.title: More than one view of the subject
checks.why: Leonardo asked for three or four views (research 01 R3, ¶798).

checks.title: No costume: the look comes with its reasons
checks.why: Research 01 §5: faux age, pseudo-mirror writing, ornamental geometry, all-over cross-hatching, many effects.

checks.title: Founder’s eye: a hand, not a plotter, not a costume — and new
checks.why: Non-negotiables 1–3 (no trend-chasing, no boring work, no shallow branding) cannot be computed. Look at the 4× crops first, then the whole sheet at phone width.
